We rewrite the equations for Gauss-Seidel iteration: From [latex] x_1 + 2x_2 + 3x_3 = 5 [/latex]: [latex] x_1 = 5 - 2x_2 - 3x_3 [/latex] From [latex] 2x_1 + 3x_2 + x_3 = 1 [/latex]: [latex] x_2 = \frac{1 - 2x_1 - x_3}{3} [/latex] From [latex] 3x_1 + 2x_2 + x_3 = 3 [/latex]: [latex] x_3 = 3 - 3x_1 - 2x_2 [/latex] First Iteration: Step 1: Compute [latex] x_1^{(1)} [/latex] Using [latex] x_2^{(0)} = 0 [/latex], [latex] x_3^{(0)} = 0 [/latex]: [latex] x_1^{(1)} = 5 - 2(0) - 3(0) = 5 [/latex] Step 2: Compute [latex] x_2^{(1)} [/latex] Using [latex] x_1^{(1)} = 5 [/latex], [latex] x_3^{(0)} = 0 [/latex]: [latex] x_2^{(1)} = \frac{1 - 2(5) - 0}{3} = \frac{1 - 10}{3} = \frac{-9}{3} = -3 [/latex] Step 3: Compute [latex] x_3^{(1)} [/latex] Using [latex] x_1^{(1)} = 5 [/latex], [latex] x_2^{(1)} = -3 [/latex]: [latex] x_3^{(1)} = 3 - 3(5) - 2(-3) = 3 - 15 + 6 = -6 [/latex] Final Answer: After the first iteration, [latex] x_3 = -6 [/latex].

From [latex] x_1 + 2x_2 + 3x_3 = 5 [/latex]:
[latex] x_1 = 5 - 2x_2 - 3x_3 [/latex]


From [latex] 2x_1 + 3x_2 + x_3 = 1 [/latex]:
[latex] x_2 = \frac{1 - 2x_1 - x_3}{3} [/latex]

From [latex] 3x_1 + 2x_2 + x_3 = 3 [/latex]:
[latex] x_3 = 3 - 3x_1 - 2x_2 [/latex]

First Iteration:
Step 1:
Compute [latex] x_1^{(1)} [/latex]
Using [latex] x_2^{(0)} = 0 [/latex], [latex] x_3^{(0)} = 0 [/latex]:
[latex] x_1^{(1)} = 5 - 2(0) - 3(0) = 5 [/latex]

Step 2: Compute [latex] x_2^{(1)} [/latex]
Using [latex] x_1^{(1)} = 5 [/latex], [latex] x_3^{(0)} = 0 [/latex]:
[latex] x_2^{(1)} = \frac{1 - 2(5) - 0}{3} = \frac{1 - 10}{3} = \frac{-9}{3} = -3 [/latex]

Step 3: Compute [latex] x_3^{(1)} [/latex]
Using [latex] x_1^{(1)} = 5 [/latex], [latex] x_2^{(1)} = -3 [/latex]:
[latex] x_3^{(1)} = 3 - 3(5) - 2(-3) = 3 - 15 + 6 = -6 [/latex]

dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_text: [latex]\begin{aligned} I &= \int_{0}^{2}\frac{(x-1)^2 \sin (x-1)}{(x-1)^2 + \cos (x-1)}dx\\ \text{Taking}\; x-1=z&\Rightarrow dx=dz \\ \text{for}\; x=0,&z\rightarrow -1\; \text{and}\; x=2, z \rightarrow 1 \\ \therefore \; I &=\int_{-1}^{1} \frac{z^2 \sin z}{z^2+\cos z}dz\\ \text{let}\;\; f(z)&=\frac{z^2 \sin z}{z^2+ \cos z} dz\\ f(-z) &= \frac{z^2 \sin z}{z^2+ \cos z}\\ f(z)&= -f(z) \; \text{function is ODD}\\ \therefore \;\; I&=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]

dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_text: As per Cauchy-Riemann equations: [latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial y} and \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-\frac{\partial v}{\partial x} [/latex] [latex] u=x^{2}-y^{2} [/latex] [latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=2 x, \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-2 y [/latex] [latex] \therefore \quad \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=2 x [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \quad v=2 x y+f(x) [/latex] [latex] \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=2 y+f(x) [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=2 y+f^{\prime}(x) [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \quad f^{\prime}(x)=0 \quad \text { i.e. } f(x)=c [/latex] [latex] \therefore \quad v=2 x y+c [/latex]
dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_html:
As per Cauchy-Riemann equations:
[latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial y} and \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-\frac{\partial v}{\partial x} [/latex]
[latex] u=x^{2}-y^{2} [/latex]
[latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=2 x, \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-2 y [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \quad \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=2 x [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad v=2 x y+f(x) [/latex]
[latex] \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=2 y+f(x) [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=2 y+f^{\prime}(x) [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad f^{\prime}(x)=0 \quad \text { i.e. } f(x)=c [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \quad v=2 x y+c [/latex]

The characteristic equation [latex] | A-\lambda D=0 [/latex]

[latex] \; [A-\lambda I] x=\left[\begin{array}{cc}-5-\lambda & 2 \\-9 & 6-\lambda\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}x \\y\end{array}\right] [/latex]
[latex] =0 [/latex]

[latex] -9 x+2 y=0 [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \frac{x}{2}=\frac{y}{9}[/latex] gives eigen vector (2,9)
Corresponding to [latex] \lambda=-3, [/latex]

which gives -x+y=0 (only one independent equation)
[latex] \therefore \quad \frac{x}{1}=\frac{y}{1} \quad [/latex] which gives (1,1)
So, the eigen vectors are [latex]\left\{\begin{array}{l}2 \\ 9\end{array}\right\} and \left\{\begin{array}{l}1 \\ 1\end{array}\right\}[/latex]

 where k is a constant, subjected to the boundary conditions  u(0) = 0  and  u(L) = U,  is
dummy_engineering_mathematics.html: The solution to the differential equation [latex]\frac{\mathrm{d^{2}u} }{\mathrm{d} x^{2}}-k\frac{\mathrm{du} }{\mathrm{d} x}=0[/latex] where k is a constant, subjected to the boundary conditions u(0) = 0 and u(L) = U, is
dummy_engineering_mathematics.subject: Engineering Mathematics - Differential Equations
dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_text: We have [latex]\frac{\mathrm{d^{2}u} }{\mathrm{d} x^{2}}-k\frac{\mathrm{du} }{\mathrm{d} x}=0[/latex] [latex](D^2-kD)u=0 [/latex] The auxiliary equation is [latex]\begin{aligned} m^2-km&=0\\ m(m-k)&=0\\ m&=0,k \end{aligned}  [/latex] Thus the complete solution is [latex]\begin{aligned} u&=C_1e^{0x}+C_2e^{kx}\\ u&=C_1+C_2e^{kx} \end{aligned}  [/latex] From given condition [latex] u(0)=0:\;\; C_1+C_2=0 \;\;\;...(i) [/latex] [latex]u(L)=U:\;\; U=C_1+C_2e^{kL}\;\;\;...(ii) [/latex] Subtracting equation (i) from (ii), we get [latex]U=C_2(e^{kL}-1) [/latex] [latex]C_2=\frac{U}{e^{kL}-1} [/latex] From equation (i), we have [latex] C_1=-C_2=\frac{-U}{e^{kL}-1} [/latex] Substitute these values in the expression for u, we get [latex] u=\frac{-U}{e^{kL}-1}+\frac{U}{e^{kL}-1}e^{kx}=U\left ( \frac{1-e^{kx}}{1-e^{kL}} \right )[/latex]
dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_html:
We have [latex]\frac{\mathrm{d^{2}u} }{\mathrm{d} x^{2}}-k\frac{\mathrm{du} }{\mathrm{d} x}=0[/latex]
[latex](D^2-kD)u=0 [/latex]
The auxiliary equation is
[latex]\begin{aligned} m^2-km&=0\\ m(m-k)&=0\\ m&=0,k \end{aligned} [/latex]
Thus the complete solution is
[latex]\begin{aligned} u&=C_1e^{0x}+C_2e^{kx}\\ u&=C_1+C_2e^{kx} \end{aligned} [/latex]
From given condition
[latex] u(0)=0:\;\; C_1+C_2=0 \;\;\;...(i) [/latex]
[latex]u(L)=U:\;\; U=C_1+C_2e^{kL}\;\;\;...(ii) [/latex]
Subtracting equation (i) from (ii), we get
[latex]U=C_2(e^{kL}-1) [/latex]
[latex]C_2=\frac{U}{e^{kL}-1} [/latex]
From equation (i), we have
[latex] C_1=-C_2=\frac{-U}{e^{kL}-1} [/latex]
Substitute these values in the expression for u, we get
[latex] u=\frac{-U}{e^{kL}-1}+\frac{U}{e^{kL}-1}e^{kx}=U\left ( \frac{1-e^{kx}}{1-e^{kL}} \right )[/latex]

The probability that a student knows the correct answer to a multiple choice question is [latex]\frac{2}{3}[/latex]

conditional probability that the student knows the correct answer is
dummy_engineering_mathematics.html: The probability that a student knows the correct answer to a multiple choice question is [latex]\frac{2}{3}[/latex] If the student does not know the answer, then the student guesses the answer. The probability of the guessed answer being correct is [latex]\frac{1}{4}[/latex] Given that the student has answered the question correctly, the conditional probability that the student knows the correct answer is
dummy_engineering_mathematics.subject: Engineering Mathematics - Probability and Statistics
dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_text: Let A be the event when student knows the answer and B be the event when student guesses the answer. Therefore [latex]P(A)=P(A\cap B)=\frac{2}{3} [/latex] [latex]P(B)=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{3}\times \frac{1}{4}=\frac{9}{12}[/latex] where [latex]\frac{2}{3}[/latex] is the probability of correct answer and [latex]\frac{1}{3}[/latex] is the probability that student does not know the answer. So guesses the answer and probability of correct guess is [latex]\frac{1}{4}[/latex]. Therefore total probability of correct answer [latex]=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{1}{4}=\frac{9}{12}[/latex] Conditional probability that student knows the correct answer [latex]P(A/B)=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}=\frac{\frac{2}{3}}{\frac{9}{12}}=\frac{8}{9}[/latex]
dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_html:
Let A be the event when student knows the answer and B be the event when student guesses the answer. Therefore
[latex]P(A)=P(A\cap B)=\frac{2}{3} [/latex]
[latex]P(B)=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{3}\times \frac{1}{4}=\frac{9}{12}[/latex]
where [latex]\frac{2}{3}[/latex] is the probability of correct answer and [latex]\frac{1}{3}[/latex] is the probability that student does not know the answer. So guesses the answer and probability of correct guess is [latex]\frac{1}{4}[/latex]. Therefore total probability of correct answer
[latex]=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{1}{4}=\frac{9}{12}[/latex]
Conditional probability that student knows the correct answer
[latex]P(A/B)=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}=\frac{\frac{2}{3}}{\frac{9}{12}}=\frac{8}{9}[/latex]

dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_text: [latex]\begin{aligned} &\begin{aligned} F(s) &=\frac{1}{s(s+1)}=\frac{A}{s}+\frac{B}{s+1} \\ &=\frac{A(s+1)+B(s)}{s(s+1)} \end{aligned}\\ &\Rightarrow A(s+1)+B(s)=0\\ &\text { Put } \quad s=0\\ &\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow & A=1 \\ \text { and } & s=-1 \end{array}\\ &\Rightarrow \quad B=-1\\ &\text { So } \quad F(s)=\frac{1}{s}-\frac{1}{s+1}\\ &\begin{aligned} \text { Now } & f(t)=L^{-1}(F(s))=e^{0 t}-e^{-t} \\ & f(t)=1-e^{-t} \end{aligned} \end{aligned}[/latex]

dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_text: [latex]x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}=1 [/latex] [latex] f(x, y, z)=x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}-1=0 [/latex] [latex] \text { grad } f=\frac{\partial f}{\partial x} \hat{i}+\frac{\partial f}{\partial y} \hat{j}+\frac{\partial f}{\partial z} \hat{k} [/latex] [latex] =2 x \hat{i}+2 y j+2 z \hat{k} [/latex] [latex] \text { at }\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, 0\right)[/latex] [latex] grad f=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} \hat{i}+\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} \hat{j}+2 \times 0 \times \hat{k} [/latex] [latex] \quad=\sqrt{2} i+\sqrt{2} j+0 \hat{k} [/latex] [latex] |grad\; f|=\sqrt{2+2}=\sqrt{4}=2 [/latex] The unit outward normal vector at point P is [latex] n=\frac{1}{|grad\;f|}(grad\;f)_{at\;p}[/latex] [latex] =\frac{1}{2}(\sqrt{2} i+\sqrt{2} j)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} j[/latex]

[latex]x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}=1 [/latex]

[latex] \quad=\sqrt{2} i+\sqrt{2} j+0 \hat{k} [/latex]
[latex] |grad\; f|=\sqrt{2+2}=\sqrt{4}=2 [/latex]
The unit outward normal vector at point P is

Characteristic equation of A is

dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_text: [latex]\text{Curve 1:} y^{2}=4 x [/latex] [latex] \text{Curve 2:} x^{2}=4 y [/latex] Intersection points of curve 1 and 2 [latex] y^{2}=4 x=4 \sqrt{4 y}=8 \sqrt{y} [/latex] [latex] y^{4}=8 \times 8 y[/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \quad y\left(y^{3}-64\right)=0 [/latex] [latex] \text { Solution } \quad y=A \text { and } y=0[/latex] [latex] then \quad x=4 \quad x=0 [/latex] Therefore intersection point are A(4,4) and 0(0,0) The area enclosed between curves' 1 and 2 are given by [latex] \begin{aligned} \text { Area } &=\int_{x_{1}}^{x_{2}}\left(y_{1}-y_{2}\right) dx=\int_{0}^{4}\left(\sqrt{4 x}-\frac{x^{2}}{4}\right) dx \\ &=2 \frac{x^{3 / 2}}{3 / 2}-\left.\frac{x^{3}}{3 \times 4}\right|_{0} ^{4} \\ &=\frac{4}{3}(4)^{3 / 2}-\frac{(4)^{3}}{3 \times 5}=\frac{16}{3} \end{aligned}[/latex]

dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_text: Let the point be the(x,y,z) The distance between two given coordinates is given as [latex] \begin{aligned} D^{2} &=\sqrt{(x-0)^{2}+(y-0)^{2}-(z-0)^{2}} \\ D^{2} &=x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2} \\ \text { given } z^{2} &=1+x y \\ D^{2} &=x^{2}+y^{2}+1+x y \end{aligned}[/latex] Let [latex]D^{2}=U [/latex] [latex] U=x^{2}+y^{2}+1+x y[/latex] For minimum or nearest distance [latex] \begin{aligned} p &=\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=0 \\ \Rightarrow 2x+y &=0 &... i \\ \Rightarrow \quad q &=\frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=0 \\ &=2y+x=0&... ii \end{aligned}[/latex] By solving equation (i) and (ii) [latex] \begin{aligned} &x=0\\ &y=0\\ &z=1\\ &\begin{aligned} r &=\frac{\partial^{2} v}{\partial x^{2}}=2 \\ t &=\frac{\partial^{2} v}{\partial y^{2}}=2 \\ s &=\frac{\partial^{2} u}{\partial x \partial y}=1 \\ r t-s^{2} &=2 \times 2-1^{2}=3 \\ r t-s^{2} &>0 \\r &>0 \end{aligned} \end{aligned}[/latex] [latex] \therefore[/latex] distance is minimum. Hence the distance should be [latex] D=\sqrt{(0-0)^{2}+(0-0)^{2}-(1-0)^{2}} [/latex] [latex] D=1 \mathrm{m}[/latex]

Let [latex]D^{2}=U [/latex]
[latex] U=x^{2}+y^{2}+1+x y[/latex]
For minimum or nearest distance

By solving equation (i) and (ii)
[latex] \begin{aligned} &x=0\\ &y=0\\ &z=1\\ &\begin{aligned} r &=\frac{\partial^{2} v}{\partial x^{2}}=2 \\ t &=\frac{\partial^{2} v}{\partial y^{2}}=2 \\ s &=\frac{\partial^{2} u}{\partial x \partial y}=1 \\ r t-s^{2} &=2 \times 2-1^{2}=3 \\ r t-s^{2} &>0 \\r &>0 \end{aligned} \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex] \therefore[/latex] distance is minimum.

dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_text: Path AB: [latex] \begin{aligned} x^{2}+y^{2} &=1 \\ x &=\cos \theta \\ y &=\sin \theta \end{aligned}[/latex] Along path AB [latex] \theta [/latex] varies from [latex]0^{\circ} \; \text { to }  \; 90^{\circ}[0 \text { to } \pi / 2] [/latex] [latex] \int_{\text {Path } A B}(x+y)^{2}(r d \theta)[/latex] [latex] =\int_{0}^{\pi / 2}(\cos \theta+\sin \theta)^{2} 1 \cdot d \theta [/latex] [latex] =\int_{0}^{\pi / 2}\left(\sin ^{2} \theta+\cos ^{2} \theta+2 \sin \theta \cos \theta\right) d \theta [/latex] [latex] =\int_{0}^{\pi / 2}(1+\sin 2 \theta) d \theta [/latex] [latex] =\theta+\left.\frac{(-\cos 2 \theta)}{2}\right|_{0} ^{\pi / 2} [/latex] [latex] =\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\left[\cos 2 \frac{\pi}{2}-\cos 0\right] [/latex] [latex] =\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{1}{2}[-1-1]=\frac{\pi}{2}+1[/latex]
dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_html:
Path AB:
[latex] \begin{aligned} x^{2}+y^{2} &=1 \\ x &=\cos \theta \\ y &=\sin \theta \end{aligned}[/latex]
Along path AB [latex] \theta [/latex] varies from [latex]0^{\circ} \; \text { to } \; 90^{\circ}[0 \text { to } \pi / 2] [/latex]
[latex] \int_{\text {Path } A B}(x+y)^{2}(r d \theta)[/latex]

[latex] =\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{1}{2}[-1-1]=\frac{\pi}{2}+1[/latex]

 is
dummy_engineering_mathematics.html: The solution of [latex]x\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+y=x^{4}[/latex] with the condition [latex]y(1)=\frac{6}{5}[/latex] is
dummy_engineering_mathematics.subject: Engineering Mathematics - Differential Equations
dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_text: Given differential equation is [latex] \begin{aligned} x \frac{d y}{d x}+y &=x^{4} \\ \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}+\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) y &=x^{3} \end{aligned}[/latex] Standard form [latex] \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}+P y=Q[/latex] where P and Q function of x only and solution is given by [latex] y(\text { I.F. })=\int Q \cdot(I F .) d x+C[/latex] where, integrating factor (I.F.)[latex] =e^{\int P d x} [/latex] [latex] \text{Here} \quad P =\frac{1}{x} \text { and } Q=x^{3} [/latex] [latex] \text { I.F. } =e^{\int \frac{1}{x} d x}=e^{\ln x}=x[/latex] Solution [latex] \quad y(x)=\int x^{3} \cdot x d x+c [/latex] [latex] y x=\frac{x^{5}}{5}+c [/latex] given condition [latex] y(1)=\frac{6}{5} [/latex] means at [latex]x=1 ; y=\frac{6}{5} [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \quad \frac{6}{5} \times 1=\frac{1}{5}+c [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \quad c=\frac{6}{5}-\frac{1}{5}=1 [/latex] Therefore [latex] y x=\frac{x^{5}}{5}+1 [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \quad y=\frac{x^{4}}{5}+\frac{1}{x}[/latex]
dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_html:
Given differential equation is
[latex] \begin{aligned} x \frac{d y}{d x}+y &=x^{4} \\ \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}+\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) y &=x^{3} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Standard form
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}+P y=Q[/latex]
where P and Q function of x only and solution is given by
[latex] y(\text { I.F. })=\int Q \cdot(I F .) d x+C[/latex]
where, integrating factor (I.F.)[latex] =e^{\int P d x} [/latex]
[latex] \text{Here} \quad P =\frac{1}{x} \text { and } Q=x^{3} [/latex]
[latex] \text { I.F. } =e^{\int \frac{1}{x} d x}=e^{\ln x}=x[/latex]
Solution [latex] \quad y(x)=\int x^{3} \cdot x d x+c [/latex]
[latex] y x=\frac{x^{5}}{5}+c [/latex]
given condition
[latex] y(1)=\frac{6}{5} [/latex]
means at [latex]x=1 ; y=\frac{6}{5} [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad \frac{6}{5} \times 1=\frac{1}{5}+c [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad c=\frac{6}{5}-\frac{1}{5}=1 [/latex]
Therefore [latex] y x=\frac{x^{5}}{5}+1 [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad y=\frac{x^{4}}{5}+\frac{1}{x}[/latex]

 where [latex]i=\sqrt{-1}[/latex]. If u = xy, the expression for v should be
dummy_engineering_mathematics.html: An analytic function of a Complex Variables z = x + iy is expressed as [latex]f(z)=u(x,y)+iv(x,y)[/latex] where [latex]i=\sqrt{-1}[/latex]. If u = xy, the expression for v should be

dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_text: [latex]\begin{aligned} u &=x y \\ u_{x} &=\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=y \\ u_{y} &=\frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=x \\ f(z) &=u(x, y)+i v(x, y) \\ f^{\prime}(z) &=u_{x}+i v_{x}=v_{y}-i u_{y} \end{aligned}[/latex] Cauchy Riemann Equation [latex] \begin{aligned} u_{x} &=v_{y} \\ v_{x} &=-u_{y} \\ f^{\prime}(z) &=u_{x}-i u_{y} \\ f^{\prime}(z) &=y-i x \\ \text{Put x=z and y}&=0\\ f^{\prime}(z) &=0-i z \\ f(z) &=\int(-i z) d z \\ f(z) &=-i \frac{z^{2}}{2}+c_{1}+i c_{2} \\ c_{1} &=0(\text { constant in real part }) \\ f(z) &=\frac{-i z^{2}}{2}+i c_{2} \\ &=\frac{-i(x+i y)^{2}}{2}+i c_{2} \\ f(z) &=x y+\frac{i\left(y^{2}-x^{2}\right)}{2}+i c_{2} \\ f(z) &=u(x, y)+i v(x, y) \end{aligned}[/latex] Comparing imaginary part [latex] \begin{aligned} v &=\frac{y^{2}-x^{2}}{2}+c_{2} \\ &=\frac{y^{2}-x^{2}}{2}+k \end{aligned}[/latex]

Cauchy Riemann Equation
[latex] \begin{aligned} u_{x} &=v_{y} \\ v_{x} &=-u_{y} \\ f^{\prime}(z) &=u_{x}-i u_{y} \\ f^{\prime}(z) &=y-i x \\ \text{Put x=z and y}&=0\\ f^{\prime}(z) &=0-i z \\ f(z) &=\int(-i z) d z \\ f(z) &=-i \frac{z^{2}}{2}+c_{1}+i c_{2} \\ c_{1} &=0(\text { constant in real part }) \\ f(z) &=\frac{-i z^{2}}{2}+i c_{2} \\ &=\frac{-i(x+i y)^{2}}{2}+i c_{2} \\ f(z) &=x y+\frac{i\left(y^{2}-x^{2}\right)}{2}+i c_{2} \\ f(z) &=u(x, y)+i v(x, y) \end{aligned}[/latex]
Comparing imaginary part
[latex] \begin{aligned} v &=\frac{y^{2}-x^{2}}{2}+c_{2} \\ &=\frac{y^{2}-x^{2}}{2}+k \end{aligned}[/latex]

dummy_engineering_mathematics.html: If three coins are tossed simultaneously, the probability of getting at least one head

dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_text: Three coins are tossed simultaneously, the total number of ways [latex] =2^{3}=8 [/latex] Number of ways to get all tails = 1 [latex] Probability to get all tails [/latex] [latex] =\frac{\text { Number of ways for tails }}{\text { Total number of ways }}=\frac{1}{8} [/latex] Therefore probability to get at least one head is [latex] =1-\frac{1}{8}=\frac{7}{8}[/latex] or, Total number of ways with at least one head is [latex] \left.\begin{matrix} & &\left.\begin{array}{lll} H & T & T \\ T & H & T \\ T & T & H \end{array} \right] \\ &&\left.\begin{array}{lll} H & T & T \\ T & H & T \\ T & T & H \end{array} \right] \\ &&\left.\begin{array}{lll} H & H & H \end{array} \right] \end{matrix}\right\}[/latex] Therefore probability to get at least one head [latex] =\frac{7}{8} [/latex]
dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_html:
Three coins are tossed simultaneously, the total
number of ways [latex] =2^{3}=8 [/latex]
Number of ways to get all tails = 1
[latex] Probability to get all tails [/latex]
[latex] =\frac{\text { Number of ways for tails }}{\text { Total number of ways }}=\frac{1}{8} [/latex]
Therefore probability to get at least one head is
[latex] =1-\frac{1}{8}=\frac{7}{8}[/latex]
or, Total number of ways with at least one head is
[latex] \left.\begin{matrix} & &\left.\begin{array}{lll} H & T & T \\ T & H & T \\ T & T & H \end{array} \right] \\ &&\left.\begin{array}{lll} H & T & T \\ T & H & T \\ T & T & H \end{array} \right] \\ &&\left.\begin{array}{lll} H & H & H \end{array} \right] \end{matrix}\right\}[/latex]
Therefore probability to get at least one head [latex] =\frac{7}{8} [/latex]

dummy_engineering_mathematics.text: Consider a continuous random variable with probability density function [latex]f(t)= 1+t[/latex]  for [latex] -1\leq t \leq 0[/latex] [latex]f(t)= 1-t[/latex] for [latex] 0\leq t \leq 1[/latex] The standard deviation of the random variable is:
dummy_engineering_mathematics.html:
Consider a continuous random variable with probability density function
[latex]f(t)= 1+t[/latex] for [latex] -1\leq t \leq 0[/latex]
[latex]f(t)= 1-t[/latex] for [latex] 0\leq t \leq 1[/latex]
The standard deviation of the random variable is:
dummy_engineering_mathematics.subject: Engineering Mathematics - Probability and Statistics
dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_text: Mean [latex] (\bar{t})=\int_{-1}^{\infty} t \cdot f(t) \cdot d t [/latex] [latex] \quad=\int_{-1}^{0} t(1+t) d t+\int_{0}^{1} t(1-t) d t [/latex] [latex] \quad=\left[\frac{t^{2}}{2}+\frac{t^{3}}{3}\right]_{-1}^{0}+\left[\frac{t^{2}}{2}-\frac{t^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{1} [/latex] [latex] \quad=-\left[\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}\right]+\left[\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}\right] [/latex] [latex] =-\left[\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{6}\right]=0 [/latex] Variance [latex]=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}(t-\bar{t})^{2} f(t) d t [/latex] [latex] =\int_{-1}^{0} t^{2}(1+t) \cdot d t+\int_{0}^{1} t^{2}(1-t) d t [/latex] [latex] =\int_{-1}^{0}\left(t^{2}+t^{3}\right) \cdot d t+\int_{0}^{1} t^{2}(1-t) d t [/latex] [latex] =\left[\frac{t^{3}}{3}+\frac{t^{4}}{4}\right]_{-1}^{0}+\left[\frac{t^{3}}{3}-\frac{t^{4}}{4}\right]_{0}^{1} [/latex] [latex] =\frac{1}{12}+\frac{1}{12}=\frac{1}{6} [/latex] Standard deviation [latex] =\sqrt{\text { variance }}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}[/latex]
dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_html:
Mean [latex] (\bar{t})=\int_{-1}^{\infty} t \cdot f(t) \cdot d t [/latex]
[latex] \quad=\int_{-1}^{0} t(1+t) d t+\int_{0}^{1} t(1-t) d t [/latex]
[latex] \quad=\left[\frac{t^{2}}{2}+\frac{t^{3}}{3}\right]_{-1}^{0}+\left[\frac{t^{2}}{2}-\frac{t^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{1} [/latex]
[latex] \quad=-\left[\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}\right]+\left[\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}\right] [/latex]
[latex] =-\left[\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{6}\right]=0 [/latex]
Variance [latex]=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}(t-\bar{t})^{2} f(t) d t [/latex]
[latex] =\int_{-1}^{0} t^{2}(1+t) \cdot d t+\int_{0}^{1} t^{2}(1-t) d t [/latex]
[latex] =\int_{-1}^{0}\left(t^{2}+t^{3}\right) \cdot d t+\int_{0}^{1} t^{2}(1-t) d t [/latex]
[latex] =\left[\frac{t^{3}}{3}+\frac{t^{4}}{4}\right]_{-1}^{0}+\left[\frac{t^{3}}{3}-\frac{t^{4}}{4}\right]_{0}^{1} [/latex]
[latex] =\frac{1}{12}+\frac{1}{12}=\frac{1}{6} [/latex]
Standard deviation
[latex] =\sqrt{\text { variance }}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}[/latex]

Consider the system of simultaneous equation

This system has

dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_text: Given equation are [latex] \begin{array}{r} x+2 y+z=6 \\ 2 x+y+2 z=6 \\ x+y+z=5 \end{array}[/latex] Given system can be written as [latex] \left[\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l} x \\ y \\ z \end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{l} 6 \\ 6 \\ 5 \end{array}\right][/latex] Applying row operation [latex] \begin{array}{l} R_{2} \rightarrow R_{2}-2 R_{1}, R_{3} \rightarrow R_{3}-R_{1} \\ {\left[\begin{array}{ccc} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l} x \\ y \\ z \end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{c} 6 \\ -6 \\ -1 \end{array}\right]} \end{array}[/latex] [latex] \text{and applying} R_{3} \rightarrow 3 R_{3}-R_{2} [/latex] [latex] \left[\begin{array}{ccc} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l} x \\ y \\ z \end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{c} 6 \\ -6 \\ 3 \end{array}\right][/latex] since the rank of coefficient matrix is 2 and rank of argument matrix is 3, which are not equal. Hence, system has no solution.
dummy_engineering_mathematics.explanation_html:
Given equation are
[latex] \begin{array}{r} x+2 y+z=6 \\ 2 x+y+2 z=6 \\ x+y+z=5 \end{array}[/latex]
Given system can be written as
[latex] \left[\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l} x \\ y \\ z \end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{l} 6 \\ 6 \\ 5 \end{array}\right][/latex]
Applying row operation
[latex] \begin{array}{l} R_{2} \rightarrow R_{2}-2 R_{1}, R_{3} \rightarrow R_{3}-R_{1} \\ {\left[\begin{array}{ccc} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l} x \\ y \\ z \end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{c} 6 \\ -6 \\ -1 \end{array}\right]} \end{array}[/latex]
[latex] \text{and applying} R_{3} \rightarrow 3 R_{3}-R_{2} [/latex]
[latex] \left[\begin{array}{ccc} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l} x \\ y \\ z \end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{c} 6 \\ -6 \\ 3 \end{array}\right][/latex]
since the rank of coefficient matrix is 2 and rank of argument matrix is 3, which are not equal. Hence, system has no solution.
